messages:
tara: Quick sync — deciding what goes into the next mini-iteration (2w). Pulled post-launch list: 1) search-timeout-regression (high impact, customers reporting), 2) conversational UX microcopy (small polish), 3) batching perf tail (sporadic high p99). Can we pick owners and a rule for cut vs ship?
omar: My rule: regressions that hit customer flows or SLAs = cut-first. Low-effort UX fixes (<=2 dev-days) can slip into the same slice; anything >2d -> backlog. :+1:
jess: Agreed. Need telemetry to estimate effort & risk. I can run an error-rate + session-sample pass and return numbers in ~3h.
matt: FYI infra bandwidth this sprint is ~1.5 dev-weeks if we deprioritize a planned infra cleanup. That could cover a 2d hotfix + 3d spike.
nana: I volunteer for search-timeout-regression. Will triage immediately and aim for a hotfix PR if root cause <=1 day; otherwise escalate.
deploy-bot: canary deploy at 2024-11-03T15:12:03Z succeeded in us-west :white_check_mark: (no errors reported in this canary window)
omar: If ana can't deliver same-day, fallback is to apply a temporary rate limit on search queries and roll back to v1 index for the highest-traffic customers.
tara: Decision summary: owner ana for reg (target hotfix within 48h), jess runs telemetry (ETA 3h), UX microcopy -> schedule as p2 into "nice-to-have" slice unless jess finds >5% drop in conversion; batching perf -> create 5d investigation spike, assign matt. I'll file a short PRD with these outcomes and ping the customer contacts. :thumbsup:
